protocol.instrument_name: Queensland Community Pharmacy Smoking Cessation - Clinical Practice Guideline
protocol.legal_basis: Not stated in this document; issued by Queensland Health as a Queensland Community Pharmacy clinical practice guideline for a prescribing service (page 1).
protocol.supervision_model: Document's own terminology: pharmacists are advised to 'exercise professional discretion and judgement' and to decide 'in consultation with the patient and/or their parent/caregiver'; pharmacists must prescribe according to 'the specified sections of the current online version of the Therapeutic Guidelines'. No 'collaborative'/'autonomous' label is printed.
protocol.scope_summary: Clinical practice guideline for pharmacist-led smoking cessation in Queensland community pharmacies. 'Service restricted to patients aged 18 years or over.' Covers tobacco smoking cessation only - the management of vaping cessation (and pharmacotherapy for vaping cessation) is not within scope. Covers 5As-based assessment, patient and smoking history, blood pressure and comorbidity screening, counselling/behavioural support, pharmacotherapy guided by the RACGP Pharmacotherapy treatment algorithm and Therapeutic Guidelines: Addiction, referral triggers and drug-specific follow-up. No drug strength, dose or frequency is printed.

inclusion.text: Service restricted to patients aged 18 years or over.

exclusion.text: the patient is taking a medicine that interacts with smoking and may require review and dose adjustment due to changing smoking patterns
the management of vaping cessation is not within the scope of this guideline
the use of pharmacotherapy for vaping cessation is not within the scope of this guideline

exclusion_exceptions.text: Ineligibility for treatment as part of a prescribing service does not preclude a patient from accessing services provided as part of usual pharmacy care.

diagnosis_pathways.name: Smoking cessation - assessment, management and follow-up pathway

steps.description: Patient history and assessment: The 5As approach is recommended to identify an individual's support needs, barriers and other relevant cultural, population-specific, or medicine-associated factors, to develop a comprehensive smoking cessation plan (2, 4).

Assessment references (continues from page 2): Refer to the Therapeutic Guidelines: Addiction (Tobacco smoking and nicotine dependence) (3) and Royal Australian College of General Practitioners (RACGP) Supporting smoking cessation: A guide for health professionals (2). Refer to Therapeutic Guidelines: Addiction (Tobacco smoking and nicotine dependence - Screening and assessment of tobacco smoking and nicotine dependence) to assist with determining nicotine dependence and whether pharmacotherapy may be appropriate (3).

Patient history: Obtain sufficient information from the patient to assess the safety and appropriateness of any recommendations and medicines. The patient history should consider: age; pregnancy and lactation status (if applicable); underlying medical conditions and chronic diseases including current (or history of) psychiatric illness (including but not limited to psychosis, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, clinically diagnosed depression and anxiety, eating disorder, substance use disorders and history of suicidal ideation, suicide related behaviour or self-harm); current or recently ceased treatments (including prescribed medicines, vitamins, herbs, other supplements and over-the-counter medicines); drug allergies/adverse drug reactions.

Smoking history: Consider: age when smoking first commenced; type of smoking e.g., cigarettes, pipes; time to first cigarette in the mornings; number of cigarettes smoked per day; cravings for a cigarette, urges to smoke or withdrawal symptoms upon stopping smoking; duration, recording past and current pack years; previous attempts to quit and periods of not smoking, including support required; previous responses to pharmacotherapy for smoking cessation.
Examination and screening: Take an initial blood pressure measurement to screen for hypertension.

Comorbidity screening (continues from page 3): It is recommended that the patient be screened for common comorbidities associated with smoking, including CVD, asthma and COPD, either as part of a chronic disease program in the Service (if eligible), or with or an appropriate healthcare provider. [Sentence transcribed as printed; wording 'or with or an appropriate healthcare provider' appears garbled in the source - see open_questions.]

Develop smoking cessation management plan: Pharmacists must ensure that they are prescribing medicines according to the specified sections of the current online version of the Therapeutic Guidelines. A comprehensive approach to smoking cessation should include counselling and behavioural support. The type of assistance should be based on the patient's willingness to quit, needs, preferences and level of nicotine dependence (2).

gates.criterion: Prescribing aligns with the specified sections of the current online version of the Therapeutic Guidelines

steps.description: Non-pharmacological interventions and support (ready-to-quit branch): Develop a cessation plan, e.g., Your quit smoking plan available on the Quit website; including identifying barriers to stopping, strategies to address barriers, and identifying and engaging social support.

Non-pharmacological interventions and support (not-ready-to-quit branch): For patients that are not ready to quit, use motivational approaches, explore barriers, and encourage harm minimisation such as reducing the number of cigarettes smoked each day and working towards a quit day (2, 5).

gates.criterion: Patient is not ready to quit

steps.description: Counselling and behavioural support and referral to Quitline and/or other support programs NB1. NB1: Resources to support counselling and behavioural support are available on the Queensland Government QuitHQ website for health professionals (6). Referral to Quitline or a relevant health professional with expertise specific to smoking cessation is recommended (2, 3).

Pharmacotherapy NB2: Guided by the Pharmacotherapy treatment algorithm in the RACGP Supporting smoking cessation: A guide for health professionals (2): A medicine mentioned in the Therapeutic Guidelines: Addiction (Tobacco smoking and nicotine dependence) (3) [printed with footnote marker: 'A medicineNB3 mentioned in ...']. NB2: This guideline covers tobacco smoking cessation, the use of pharmacotherapy for vaping cessation is not within the scope of this guideline. NB3: Nortriptyline or nicotine vaping products are not permitted for use by pharmacists(3).

gates.criterion: Nicotine dependence determined and pharmacotherapy may be appropriate (per Therapeutic Guidelines: Addiction - Screening and assessment of tobacco smoking and nicotine dependence)

steps.description: Confirm management is appropriate: Consult the Therapeutic Guidelines, Australian Medicines Handbook and other resources (including relevant product information) to confirm the smoking cessation plan is appropriate, including for: contraindications and precautions; drug interactions NB1; pregnancy and lactation.

gates.criterion: Contraindications and precautions, drug interactions, and pregnancy and lactation confirmed appropriate against Therapeutic Guidelines, Australian Medicines Handbook, product information and other resources

steps.description: Confirm management is appropriate - NB1 (continues from page 4): Both smoking itself and pharmacotherapy to assist with smoking cessation are associated with a number of drug interactions that require consideration when someone is deciding to reduce and/or cease smoking (7).

Communicate agreed management plan: Comprehensive advice and counselling (including supporting written information if required), should be provided to the patient regarding the smoking cessation plan. Relevant information may include: instructions for individual dosage form and medicine use e.g., medicine dosage and NRT product selection and use; how to manage adverse effects, including serious adverse effects requiring medical care e.g., mood disturbances; when to return for follow-up. It is the pharmacist's responsibility to ensure the suitability and accuracy of any resources and information provided to patients (and/or parents/caregivers if applicable) and to ensure compliance with all copyright conditions. The agreed management plan should be shared with members of the patient's multidisciplinary healthcare team, with the patient's consent.

General advice: The most successful approach to smoking cessation for nicotine dependent people is counselling and behavioural support, combined with first-line pharmacotherapy and follow-up (2). While pharmacotherapy for smoking cessation has good efficacy, relapse is not uncommon. People should be advised not to be discouraged by unsuccessful attempts and reassured that most people that have previously smoked have progressed through a number of quitting attempts and relapses before achieving long-term cessation (3). Patients should be advised to seek support from an appropriate healthcare provider and a smoking cessation service (e.g. Quitline) if they relapse, or at any time they require extra assistance or have any concerns.

Clinical review: Clinical review with the pharmacist (or the patient's chosen healthcare provider) should occur in line with recommendations in the Therapeutic Guidelines, the RACGP Supporting smoking cessation: A guide for health professionals and the Australian Medicines Handbook: Nicotine dependence (2, 3, 7).

Clinical review (continues from page 5) - NRT: Patients prescribed NRT should return for a follow up consultation 2 weeks after starting treatment to review for tolerability and effectiveness, and additionally at regular intervals during the minimum 12-week course (3).

Clinical review - varenicline or bupropion: Patients prescribed varenicline or bupropion should return for a follow up consultation 2 weeks after commencing treatment to monitor for progress and adverse effects of pharmacotherapy, to measure blood pressure, and to provide additional support (particularly for relapse prevention) (3). An additional follow up consultation should occur at the end of the treatment course (9 weeks for bupropion, 12 weeks for varenicline) (3). An additional 12 weeks of treatment with varenicline may be considered if required, to reduce chances of relapse.

Varenicline course limit: People who have already undergone 2 courses of varenicline (24 weeks) within the previous 12 months, or those who require additional treatment with varenicline after 2 courses should be referred to an appropriate healthcare provider.

gates.criterion: Patient has already undergone 2 courses of varenicline (24 weeks) within the previous 12 months, or requires additional treatment with varenicline after 2 courses

steps.description: It is recommended that the patient also receive follow up and ongoing support from a smoking cessation service such as Quitline. For patients continuing therapy, follow-up should be individualised to the patient's clinical presentation, response to treatment, and therapeutic goals.

Supply quantity rule: Pharmacists should prescribe a quantity of medicine (including repeats), that aligns with the expected duration of therapy, ensuring sufficient supply until the patient's next review.

open_questions.observed: The document labels these situations 'Refer when', not 'exclusion criteria'. EXC-1 to EXC-3 are transcribed as exclusions because referral means the patient is not managed solely within the prescribing service (p.1: 'Ineligibility for treatment as part of a prescribing service does not preclude a patient from accessing services provided as part of usual pharmacy care'). 'Treat (if clinically appropriate) and concurrently refer' (chronic disease/medical condition) is kept as a red flag only, not an exclusion, because treatment proceeds.
open_questions.why_unclear: Framing of refer-when bullets as eligibility exclusions is an interpretation; recorded for review.

open_questions.observed: Two separate groups were formed: refer-when bullets EXC-1..EXC-3 (read as independent any_of triggers) and scope exclusions EXC-4/EXC-5 (vaping, read as any_of). The document prints no AND/OR combinatorics for either list.
open_questions.why_unclear: No explicit combinatorics stated in the document; any_of chosen because each bullet reads as a standalone situation.

open_questions.observed: The only printed eligibility-positive statement is 'Service restricted to patients aged 18 years or over.' (p.1). No inclusion criterion such as 'patient smokes tobacco' or 'patient wishes to quit' is printed; none was inferred. EXE-1 records the ineligibility/usual-care statement.
open_questions.why_unclear: Guideline contains no inclusion-criteria section beyond the age restriction.

open_questions.observed: 'It is recommended that the patient be screened for common comorbidities associated with smoking, including CVD, asthma and COPD, either as part of a chronic disease program in the Service (if eligible), or with or an appropriate healthcare provider.' The phrase 'or with or an appropriate healthcare provider' appears garbled in the source text.
open_questions.why_unclear: Sentence is malformed in the extraction; transcribed verbatim and step marked confidence medium rather than silently repaired.

open_questions.observed: 'Take an initial blood pressure measurement to screen for hypertension' (p.3) and follow-up instructions 'to measure blood pressure' (p.6) are given, but no numeric threshold, no action on an abnormal reading, and no hypertension management step are printed.
open_questions.why_unclear: No structured trigger can be derived without inventing a threshold.

open_questions.topic: Branch routing for readiness to quit
open_questions.observed: The document gives a ready/not-ready branch: 'Develop a cessation plan...' and 'For patients that are not ready to quit, use motivational approaches...'. Step routing (on_fail SEE_PW-1-S9 / SEE_PW-1-S8) was mapped to those two printed instructions; no step ids or on-fail actions are printed.
open_questions.why_unclear: Branch content is printed but the routing notation is not; mapping inferred.

open_questions.observed: 'The most successful approach to smoking cessation for nicotine dependent people is counselling and behavioural support, combined with first-line pharmacotherapy and follow-up (2).' The document never names which agent(s) constitute first-line pharmacotherapy; per-drug first_line flags are therefore false except the algorithm-level pharmacotherapy row (TX-1).
open_questions.why_unclear: First-line status per drug is not printed.

open_questions.observed: No strength, dose, frequency or quantity is printed anywhere in the guideline. Pharmacotherapy is delegated to 'A medicine mentioned in the Therapeutic Guidelines: Addiction (Tobacco smoking and nicotine dependence)' guided by the RACGP Pharmacotherapy treatment algorithm; NRT product selection and medicine dosage are referred to counselling content only. Drug-specific durations (minimum 12-week NRT course; 9-week bupropion course; 12-week varenicline course) are the only numeric treatment parameters printed.
open_questions.why_unclear: Dosing detail does not exist in the source; treatment dose fields intentionally left blank rather than filled from outside sources.

open_questions.observed: Document gives one referral destination - 'an appropriate healthcare provider and smoking cessation support service (e.g. Quitline)' - plus patient advice to seek support 'if they relapse, or at any time they require extra assistance or have any concerns'. No urgent or emergency referral wording appears anywhere; urgent[] and emergency[] are genuinely empty.
open_questions.why_unclear: No tiered referral destinations are printed.

open_questions.observed: 'the patient is pregnant' is a refer-when trigger (p.2) and 'pregnancy and lactation' must be checked under Confirm management is appropriate (p.4), but the document prints no pregnancy- or lactation-specific smoking cessation pharmacotherapy guidance; patient history asks for 'pregnancy and lactation status (if applicable)' (p.3).
open_questions.why_unclear: No verbatim pregnancy/lactation treatment caveat exists to transcribe; content delegated to Therapeutic Guidelines/AMH.

open_questions.observed: Whole document reviewed (pp.1-9): no notifiable condition, GP notification, AIR entry or other notification requirement is mentioned. notifiable.required recorded as null.
open_questions.why_unclear: Document is silent; no page can be cited for a positive requirement.

open_questions.observed: 'Pharmacists must ensure that they are prescribing medicines according to the specified sections of the current online version of the Therapeutic Guidelines' (p.4), 'Confirm management is appropriate ... contraindications and precautions; drug interactions NB1; pregnancy and lactation' (p.4), and the pharmacotherapy gate 'whether pharmacotherapy may be appropriate' (p.3) do not state on-fail actions; recorded as on_fail 'unclear'.
open_questions.why_unclear: Spec requires on_fail; the document does not say what happens on failure.
